newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Metals - Steel, aluminium prices up.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Metals - Steel, aluminium prices up.

text.p: Taiwan aluminium ingot and steel prices were rising on Tuesday due to firming aluminium import premiums and China Steel Corp's planned third-quarter price hikes, local metal traders said.
Taiwan aluminium ingot prices were at T49.00 per kg, up from T$48.50 per kg two weeks ago, metal traders said.

Traders attributed the higher ingots prices to market anticipation of higher third-quarter aluminium import premiums that are expected to be offered at U$95-100 per tonne over LME futures, up from $84-89 per tonne in the second quarter.
Steel products rose because the island's largest producer, China Steel Corp, announced its third-quarter steel price increases on May 21.
China Steel's third-quarter hot and cold rolled steel prices were fixed atT$10.75 and T$13.85 per kg, up from T$10.35 and T$13.35 per kg, respectively.
